learningObjective: Diagnose fairness issues in multi-tenant LLM serving and identify levers that improve fairness without collapsing throughput.

canonicalClaims.claim: Multi-tenant fairness under bursty long-prompt loads is addressed by combining chunked prefill (interleave long prefill with short-tenant decode), per-tenant KV/admission quotas (cap contention), and fairness-aware scheduling; naïve serialization sacrifices too much throughput.
conditions: Serving stack supports chunked prefill + admission control.
nonImplications: Does not imply zero cost for any mitigation.
Does not imply the mix is universal; tuning depends on tenant SLA classes.

misconceptions.claim: Serializing tenants is the correct way to achieve fairness.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Serialization eliminates interference but also aggregate throughput; not a real serving option.
Per-chunk overhead is small but nonzero; too many small chunks can waste cycles.

misconceptions.claim: Per-tenant KV quotas eliminate all bursts.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Quotas cap worst-case, but a single tenant's traffic within its quota can still cause internal preemption.

implementationFacts: SGLang scheduler supports per-tenant priorities and chunked prefill.
vLLM offers admission control via max_num_seqs and max_num_batched_tokens.
performanceScenarios: The combination of chunked prefill + admission + fair queueing yields robust multi-tenant SLA in production.
